events.title: Valentina Tereshkova Becomes First Woman in Space
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6 and orbited Earth 48 times over nearly three days, becoming the first woman to travel into space.
events.significance: Her flight was a milestone for gender equality in space exploration and a major achievement in the Cold War space race. No other woman flew solo in space for decades.

events.title: Soweto Uprising Begins
events.description: Thousands of Black South African schoolchildren in Soweto protested against the mandatory use of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. Police opened fire on the demonstrators, killing hundreds of people over the following days, including 13-year-old Hector Pieterson.
events.significance: The uprising galvanized international opposition to apartheid and intensified resistance within South Africa. June 16 is now commemorated as Youth Day in South Africa.

events.title: Ford Motor Company Incorporated
events.description: Henry Ford and a group of investors incorporated the Ford Motor Company in Detroit, Michigan, with initial capital of $28,000.
events.significance: Ford went on to introduce the Model T and the moving assembly line, revolutionizing mass production and making automobiles accessible to ordinary people.

events.title: Lincoln Delivers 'House Divided' Speech
events.description: Abraham Lincoln accepted the Illinois Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in Springfield and delivered his famous speech declaring that 'a house divided against itself cannot stand.'
events.significance: The speech framed the national debate over slavery and raised Lincoln's profile, helping set the stage for his 1860 presidential run.

events.title: United States and Hawaii Annexation Treaty Signed
events.description: The United States signed a treaty of annexation with the Republic of Hawaii, setting in motion the process of incorporating the islands into U.S. territory.
events.significance: The move led to Hawaii's annexation in 1898 and extended American strategic presence in the Pacific, eventually leading to statehood in 1959.
